title: Derivation of Mechanical Energy Conservation from Work-Energy Principle
assumptions: Net work decomposed into conservative and non-conservative components: W_net = W_c + W_nc
starting_principles: Potential energy definition W_c = - Delta U

ordered_steps.explanation: Decompose total work into conservative forces W_c and non-conservative forces W_nc.
Substitute W_net = Delta K from the work-energy theorem.
Substitute W_c = - Delta U from the potential energy definition and rearrange terms.
ordered_steps.equation_latex: -\Delta U + W_{\text{nc}} = \Delta K \implies \Delta K + \Delta U = W_{\text{nc}} \implies \Delta(K + U) = W_{\text{nc}}

ordered_steps.explanation: When non-conservative work vanishes (W_nc = 0), mechanical energy is strictly invariant.
ordered_steps.equation_latex: \Delta(K + U) = 0 \implies K_i + U_i = K_f + U_f = E_{\text{mech}} = \text{constant}

limiting_cases: If non-conservative dissipative work is negative W_nc = - Q_diss, E_f = E_i - Q_diss (mechanical energy decreases)
claim_traces: HCV1 Ch 8 p. 139; HRW Ch 8 p. 209; UP Ch 7 p. 237
